items.title: The Demon's Question
items.question: A demon whispers that this exact life — every pain, every joy — will recur infinitely, identically. Offered as a test of one's life, what does your reaction reveal?
choices: How affirmable your life feels to you
items.correctAnswer: How affirmable your life feels to you
items.correctExplanation: How affirmable your life feels — crushing weight or divine gladness measures whether you'd re-sign existence. Recurrence is a scale, not a cosmology.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is how affirmable your life feels to you. The demon asks no belief, only response: gnashing versus blessing diagnoses the lived life. Cosmology undecided, ethics delivered — the thought experiment works regardless of physics.
items.lessonContent:
Reactions diagnose lives better than arguments do.
Eternal return weighs moments, not worlds.
Blessing-versus-gnashing is the honest scale.
Thought experiments bypass belief to reach valuation.
Share this: ask one moment if it deserves eternity.

items.title: The Loving Fate
items.question: Amor fati — love of fate — demands wanting nothing in life different: not past wounds, not present limits. What stance does it take toward suffering?
choices: Loving even suffering as necessary to the whole
Avoiding future pain at any price
Blaming fate for every wound received
items.correctAnswer: Loving even suffering as necessary to the whole
items.correctExplanation: Loving even suffering as necessary — amor fati wills the whole composition, dissonance included. No excerpting, no revision: the piece entire.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is loving even suffering as necessary to the whole. Erasure edits, avoidance shrinks, blame accuses — love alone affirms. The wound belongs to the music; cutting bars ruins symphonies.
items.lessonContent:
Wholes include dissonances essentially.
Editing fate falsifies the composition.
Love affirms where blame accuses.
No-excerpt policies make heavy wholes bearable.
Share this: love one unchangeable bar today.

items.title: The Dead God
items.question: 'God is dead' announces an event, not a murder: the highest values have lost binding force in European culture. What follows from this diagnosis?
choices: Proof that no gods ever existed
A scientific ban on all rituals
A crisis of meaning requiring new value-creation
items.correctAnswer: A crisis of meaning requiring new value-creation
items.correctExplanation: A meaning crisis demanding creation — dead foundations leave nihilism unless new values are built. Diagnosis convenes legislators, not mourners.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a crisis of meaning requiring new value-creation. Conversions, proofs, and bans miss the point: the ground moved, and architects are summoned. Nihilism is the unmanaged interim, not the destination.
items.lessonContent:
Dead foundations summon architects, not mourners.
Diagnosis differs from celebration entirely.
Unmanaged interims curdle into nihilism.
Value-creation is the prescribed labor.
Share this: build one small value this week.

items.title: The Two Moralities
items.question: Master morality begins in noble self-affirmation (good versus base); slave morality begins in the powerless condemning strength (good versus evil). What separates their starting points?
choices: Noble self-affirmation versus ressentiment of the powerless
items.correctAnswer: Noble self-affirmation versus ressentiment of the powerless
items.correctExplanation: Self-affirmation versus ressentiment — masters value from fullness, slaves from revenge. Origins shape content: celebration begets virtues, grievance begets prohibitions.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is noble self-affirmation versus ressentiment of the powerless. Centuries, maps, and pulpits miss it: one morality says yes to itself first, the other says no to another first. Starting gestures echo through whole systems.
items.lessonContent:
Starting gestures echo through whole systems.
Yes-to-self differs from no-to-others foundationally.
Fullness celebrates; grievance prohibits.
Trace any morality to its first movement.
Share this: spot one no-first valuation today.

items.title: The Resentful Creation
items.question: Slave morality is born, Nietzsche argues, from ressentiment — repressed revenge that cannot act and so inverts values instead. What does this feeling manufacture?
choices: A morality condemning the strong as evil
items.correctAnswer: A morality condemning the strong as evil
items.correctExplanation: A morality condemning strength as evil — impotence baptized as virtue, power denounced as sin. Revenge delayed becomes revenge moralized.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a morality condemning the strong as evil. Unexercised revenge doesn't vanish; it legislates. Meekness praised is often muscle envied — genealogy unmasks the swap.
items.lessonContent:
Delayed revenge legislates instead of striking.
Praised meekness may be envied muscle.
Impotence baptized passes for virtue.
Unmask swaps before honoring verdicts.
Share this: detect one revenge-moralized claim.

items.title: The Growing Will
items.question: Will to power names Nietzsche's basic drive — not mere domination but growth, overcoming, discharge of strength. What does this will fundamentally seek?
items.correctAnswer: Expansion and overcoming of resistance
items.correctExplanation: Expansion and overcoming — life asserting more life against resistance. Domination is one dialect; creation, mastery, and play are others.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is expansion and overcoming of resistance. Offices, luxuries, and obedience are narrow currencies of a universal spending: strength discharging against obstacles. Read power as verb (overcoming), never just noun (position).
items.lessonContent:
Power verbs (overcoming) beat power nouns (office).
Resistance is the will's necessary gymnasium.
Growth generalizes domination's narrow case.
Strength spends itself against obstacles.
Share this: overcome one resistance deliberately.

items.title: The Overcoming Figure
items.question: The Übermensch overcomes man as man overcame the ape — legislating values after the old tablets break. What kind of figure is this?
choices: A goal and self-overcoming, not a biological rank
A political office to be elected
items.correctAnswer: A goal and self-overcoming, not a biological rank
items.correctExplanation: A goal, not a rank — direction ('overcome!') rather than species. Misreadings breed supermen fantasies; the text summons self-surpassing.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is a goal and self-overcoming, not a biological rank. No breeding program, no ballot, no resurrection: a rope stretched between beast and beyond, crossed by creating values. Read rope, not race.
items.lessonContent:
Ropes indicate directions, never pedigrees.
Overcome is imperative, not description.
Value-creation is the crossing action.
Misread goals as ranks at civilization's peril.
Share this: cross one rope-segment today.

items.title: The Blinking Herd
items.question: The last men have abolished poverty, war, and gods — and with them all aspiration. 'We have invented happiness,' they blink. What does this portrait warn against?
items.correctAnswer: Contentment without aspiration
items.correctExplanation: Contentment without aspiration — comforts kept, horizons deleted. The last man is modernity's selfie: safe, smug, finished.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is contentment without aspiration. Tools, votes, and books are innocent; the blink is the indictment — no questioning, no longing, no beyond. Happiness inventoried replaces happiness pursued.
items.lessonContent:
Comforts kept can delete horizons.
Blinking replaces questioning at civilization's end.
Inventoried happiness differs from pursued joy.
Aspiration is the attic modernity sealed.
Share this: unblink at one horizon today.

items.title: The Twin Gods
items.question: Apollo supplies form, dream, and individuation; Dionysus supplies ecstasy, dissolution, and music. Greek tragedy fuses both. What does each god contribute?
choices: Form and boundary versus rapture and dissolution
items.correctAnswer: Form and boundary versus rapture and dissolution
items.correctExplanation: Form versus rapture — Apollo individuates, Dionysus dissolves; tragedy needs sculpted frenzy. One god alone makes decoration or orgy, never art.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is form and boundary versus rapture and dissolution. Moral, rational, and temporal framings moralize what is aesthetic: dreams need waking, ecstasy needs shape. Great art marries the twins.
items.lessonContent:
Great art marries form to frenzy.
Individuation needs periodic dissolution.
Single gods make decoration or orgy.
Aesthetic twins precede moral categories.
Share this: wed one form to one frenzy.

items.title: The Many Eyes
items.question: 'There are no facts, only interpretations' — perspectivism denies any view from nowhere. Done honestly, what does this yield?
items.correctAnswer: Objectivity as multiplicity of perspectives
items.correctExplanation: Objectivity as multiplicity — more eyes, different eyes, fuller seeing. Perspectivism disciplines knowledge; it never licenses fantasy.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is objectivity as multiplicity of perspectives. Denying the God's-eye view multiplies required viewpoints instead of abolishing standards. Relativism excuses; perspectivism recruits.
items.lessonContent:
More eyes see more completely, always.
God's-eye denial recruits viewpoints, not whims.
Relativism excuses; perspectivism disciplines.
Fullness grows with perspectives added.
Share this: add one eye to one issue.

items.title: The Worn Metaphors
items.question: Truths are 'illusions of which we have forgotten that they are illusions' — metaphors worn smooth by long use. What does this claim about concepts?
choices: Concepts are metaphors hardened by use
items.correctAnswer: Concepts are metaphors hardened by use
items.correctExplanation: Metaphors hardened by use — coins worn smooth: the embossing (live metaphor) effaced by circulation. Usefulness survives; literalness was never there.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is concepts are metaphors hardened by use. Forgetting the figurative origin lets abstractions pose as discoveries. Coins still spend; just remember they were minted.
items.lessonContent:
Abstractions pose as discoveries too easily.
Circulation effaces live metaphor daily.
Usefulness survives literalness never-had.
Remember minting while spending coins.
Share this: unforget one metaphor today.

items.title: The Moral Excavation
items.question: Genealogy traces moral concepts to contingent histories — debt, punishment, priestly power — rather than timeless reason. What method is this?
choices: Explaining values by their contingent origins
items.correctAnswer: Explaining values by their contingent origins
items.correctExplanation: Explaining values by contingent origins — showing how 'good' and 'guilty' were made, not found. Histories humble eternal pretensions.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is explaining values by their contingent origins. Roots help, polls describe, logic derives — genealogy narrates the accidents that pose as necessities. Made-things can be remade.
items.lessonContent:
Accidents posing as necessities invite narration.
Made values can be remade deliberately.
Histories humble eternal pretensions.
Ask how before asking whether.
Share this: historicize one sacred value.

items.title: The Inward Cruelty
items.question: Bad conscience forms when cruelty, blocked from outward discharge by society, turns back on its bearer. Genealogically, what is guilt?
choices: Internalized cruelty turned against the self
items.correctAnswer: Internalized cruelty turned against the self
items.correctExplanation: Internalized cruelty — caged instincts lacerate their keeper. Guilt is savagery with no exit but inward.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is internalized cruelty turned against the self. Voices, compasses, and digestions mystify a hydraulic fact: blocked discharge floods inward. Civilization's price is paid in self-laceration.
items.lessonContent:
Blocked discharge floods inward always.
Cages convert savagery to conscience.
Hydraulics precede moralizing explanations.
Savagery needs exits, not sermons.
Share this: build one outward channel today.

items.title: The Gazing Lesson
items.question: 'Whoever fights monsters should see to it that he does not become one. When you gaze into the abyss, the abyss gazes also into you.' What is warned against?
choices: Struggle against evil adopting evil's shape
items.correctAnswer: Struggle against evil adopting evil's shape
items.correctExplanation: Struggle adopting evil's shape — methods infect aims; hunters learn the monster's tread. Vigilance must watch the watcher too.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is struggle against evil adopting evil's shape. Resistance stays mandatory; contamination is the warned cost. Abysses teach their students regardless of curriculum — study monsters without enrolling.
items.lessonContent:
Methods infect aims silently always.
Hunters learn treads they track.
Watchers need watching most of all.
Resist without enrolling in evil's school.
Share this: check one method for contagion.

items.title: The Three Changes
items.question: Spirit becomes camel (kneeling for burdens), then lion (roaring No to duty), then child (innocent new beginning). What journey do the stages map?
items.correctAnswer: Burden, rebellion, and new beginning
items.correctExplanation: Burden, rebellion, beginning — reverence learns weight, strength learns refusal, innocence learns creation. The child plays where the lion only negated.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is burden, rebellion, and new beginning. Calendars, careers, and aging miss the logic: Yes-bearing, then No-roaring, then play-creating. Negation clears ground that only innocence builds on.
items.lessonContent:
Negation clears what innocence builds on.
Yes-bearing precedes No-roaring developmentally.
Play crowns struggles that refusal began.
Stages sequence spiritually, never chronologically.
Share this: play where you once only refused.

items.title: The Self Command
items.question: 'Become who you are' orders self-creation through self-discovery — neither copying the herd nor obeying a fixed essence. What does it reject?
choices: Both herd conformity and fixed essence
items.correctAnswer: Both herd conformity and fixed essence
items.correctExplanation: Both conformity and essence — becoming navigates between imitation and fatalism. The self is task, neither template nor tombstone.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is both herd conformity and fixed essence. Copies abdicate; essences excuse — becoming demands originals without blueprints. Task-selves beat given-selves and borrowed-selves alike.
items.lessonContent:
Selves are tasks, never templates or tombstones.
Copies abdicate; essences excuse equally.
Originals need no blueprints to begin.
Navigate between imitation and fatalism.
Share this: author one unborrowed hour.

items.title: The Eternity Test
items.question: Applied as ethics, recurrence asks of every act: would you will this moment infinitely? What does the test measure?
items.correctAnswer: Whether the moment deserves eternity
items.correctExplanation: Whether the moment deserves eternity — infinite weight crushes trivia and crowns devotion. Decide as if forever watches.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is whether the moment deserves eternity. Profits, applause, and statutes weigh nothing on infinite scales; only affirmability registers. Eternity-tests bankrupt the trivial instantly.
items.lessonContent:
Infinite weight crowns devotion, crushes trivia.
Eternity-tests bankrupt small motives fast.
Affirmability is the only valid currency.
Decide as if forever watches you.
Share this: eternity-test one habit today.

items.title: The Ranked World
items.question: With moral facts denied, Nietzsche keeps valuations: life must rank, prefer, overcome. What remains standing after facts fall?
items.correctAnswer: Interpretations and rank-orderings of value
items.correctExplanation: Interpretations and rankings — anti-realism about facts, passion for rank. Life ranks or rots; neutrality is slow death.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is interpretations and rank-orderings of value. Indifference, proofs, and commandments all miss the survivor: valuing without foundations. Standpoints persist where facts evaporated.
items.lessonContent:
Valuing survives foundations' collapse.
Rank or rot: life's standing order.
Neutrality is slow death by abstention.
Standpoints persist past evaporated facts.
Share this: rank one thing unapologetically.

items.title: The Great Reversal
items.question: Revaluation of values means overturning slave morality's verdicts — calling good what was condemned as evil, affirming becoming over being. What gets overturned?
items.correctAnswer: Life-denying moral verdicts
items.correctExplanation: Life-denying verdicts — strength, health, and becoming revalued upward; pity, humility, and stasis demoted. Tables turn, not planets.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is life-denying moral verdicts. Physics, ballots, and grammar stand untouched; only valuations rotate. Revaluation legislates morals, never nature.
items.lessonContent:
Tables turn while planets keep spinning.
Valuations rotate; nature stands pat.
Strength revalued upward heals cultures.
Legislate morals, never physics.
Share this: reverse one life-denying verdict.

items.title: The Whole Yes
items.question: Dionysian wisdom affirms existence entire — terror with rapture, destruction with creation. What scope does this yes cover?
items.correctAnswer: Existence entire, suffering included
items.correctExplanation: Existence entire — partial yeses are disguised nos. Terror belongs to the festival; excluding it cancels attendance.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is existence entire, suffering included. Selective affirmation smuggles rejection: yes-to-joy plus no-to-pain equals decorated nihilism. Festivals include storms or they are picnics.
items.lessonContent:
Partial yeses are disguised refusals.
Storms belong to festivals essentially.
Terror-included distinguishes affirmation from picnic.
Wholes or nothing: the Dionysian tariff.
Share this: yes one terror today.

items.title: The Neighbor Law
items.question: Herd instinct moralizes neighbor-love while punishing anyone who stands out — conscience as social reflex. What does it enforce?
items.correctAnswer: Conformity as conscience
items.correctExplanation: Conformity as conscience — the 'thou shalt not stand out' preaching as virtue. Neighbors applaud mirrors, never windows.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is conformity as conscience. Altruism, rebellion, and solitude all miss the mechanism: social reflex baptized as ethics. Standing out feels like sin because herds school guilt.
items.lessonContent:
Social reflexes baptize themselves as ethics.
Mirrors applauded; windows punished consistently.
Standing out feels sinful by schooling.
Conscience needs auditing for herd content.
Share this: stand out microscopically today.

items.title: The Useful Forgetting
items.question: Active forgetfulness — the power to close the doors of consciousness — is necessary for action, cheer, and health. Why must minds forget?
choices: The past never happened at all
items.correctAnswer: Rumination would paralyze all acting
items.correctExplanation: Rumination would paralyze acting — undigested pasts jam every present. Forgetting is digestion: closed doors let rooms be lived in.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is rumination would paralyze all acting. False-memory, never-happened, and storage theories misdiagnose: the issue is function, not capacity. Doors must close for rooms to be inhabitable.
items.lessonContent:
Digestion needs closed doors behind it.
Unforgotten pasts jam all presents.
Forgetting is active faculty, not failure.
Inhabitable rooms need shut doors.
Share this: close one door deliberately.

items.title: The Living Dangerously
items.question: 'Build your cities on the slopes of Vesuvius' — live dangerously, risking comfort for intensity. What does chosen danger supply?
items.correctAnswer: Stakes that make life vivid
items.correctExplanation: Stakes that make life vivid — danger concentrates existence the way lenses concentrate light. Safety diffuses; risk focuses.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is stakes that make life vivid. Riches, applause, and immunity miss the yield entirely: intensity itself is the dividend. Vesuvius slopes grow the most awake citizens.
items.lessonContent:
Intensity is danger's true dividend.
Lenses concentrate; safety diffuses.
Stakes focus existence sharply.
Awake beats secure on every ledger.
Share this: risk one comfort for vividness.

items.title: The Stronger Paradox
items.question: 'What does not kill me makes me stronger' circulates as gym wisdom. Faithful to Nietzsche, what is its actual scope?
items.correctAnswer: Some sufferings strengthen; others destroy
items.correctExplanation: Some strengthen, others destroy — dosage, constitution, and meaning decide. Slogans universalize what texts particularize.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is some sufferings strengthen while others destroy. Gym wisdom flattens a conditional claim into a poster: many break exactly where posters promise growth. Read scope before repeating maxims.
items.lessonContent:
Slogans flatten conditional claims daily.
Dosage, constitution, meaning decide outcomes.
Posters promise what texts particularize.
Read scope before repeating maxims.
Share this: scope one slogan honestly.

items.title: The Dark Consolation
items.question: Nietzsche wrote that the thought of suicide gets one through many a bad night. What function does he grant this thought?
choices: An exit that makes endurance voluntary
items.correctAnswer: An exit that makes endurance voluntary
items.correctExplanation: An exit making endurance voluntary — the door's existence converts staying into choosing. Consolation, not commandment.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is an exit that makes endurance voluntary. Duties, proofs, and sins misread entirely: the open door transforms suffered nights into chosen ones. Freedom's margin consoles without commanding.
items.lessonContent:
Open doors convert suffering into choosing.
Voluntary endurance differs from trapped pain.
Margins console without commanding exits.
Freedom's edge steadies midnight hours.
Share this: note one door that steadies you.
